title: RFP Response Library (Master Draft) — Enterprise Security Enablement Kit
content:
LAST UPDATED: 2026-02-24 (Draft)
OWNER: Talia Benson (Program Mgmt)
INTENDED USE: Internal copy blocks for questionnaires / RFPs / security addenda. Paste into customer docs as needed.

READ THIS FIRST (IMPORTANT)
- Use only language from this library (or Confluence canonical pages) when answering RFPs.
- Do not promise roadmap items. If a question asks for a control we do not support, use the “Exceptions / Alternatives” block and escalate per the exceptions policy.
- When a response differs by deployment mode, pick the correct variant:
  - Hosted API (Redwood-managed)
  - Dedicated (single-tenant/dedicated capacity; Redwood-managed runtime + agreed isolation)
  - Private (customer VPC / on-prem; shared responsibility shifts)
- Evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test letter, subprocessor list, etc.) is provided only via the evidence request playbook and typically under NDA.

QUICK PLACEHOLDERS (EDIT BEFORE SENDING)
- [CUSTOMER_NAME]
- [DEPLOYMENT_MODE: HOSTED | DEDICATED | PRIVATE]
- [REGION(S)]
- [RETENTION_SETTING / CONTRACTUAL TERMS]
- [SIEM DESTINATION]
- [IDP: Okta | Azure AD | Ping | Google Workspace | Other]
- [TICKET/DEAL ID]

APPROVAL STATUS (AS OF LAST UPDATED)
- Generally safe for RFP use: sections marked ✅
- Requires Security/GRC check: sections marked ⚠️ (common when customer asks for specifics like timelines, frequency, or contractual terms)
- Do not use without explicit approval: sections marked ⛔

==============================
1) COMPANY SECURITY PROGRAM / GOVERNANCE
==============================

1.1 ✅ Overview (high-level)
"Redwood Inference maintains a security program designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of our systems and customer data. Our program includes documented security policies and standards, security training, access control governance, vulnerability management, incident response processes, and continuous monitoring. We regularly assess the effectiveness of controls through internal reviews and independent third-party audits."

1.2 ✅ Security organization & ownership
"Security is led by the CISO (Dr. Aisha Rahman) with a dedicated Security Engineering function and a Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) function. Security and GRC partner with Engineering, Product, and Customer Success to manage risk and support customer security reviews."

1.3 ⚠️ Security training
"Redwood provides security awareness training to personnel and reinforces secure handling of customer and company information. Role-appropriate training is provided for teams with elevated access (e.g., Security, SRE)." 
Notes: Do not commit to specific training cadence unless confirmed for the period in scope.

1.4 ⚠️ Risk management
"Redwood maintains a risk management process that includes identifying, assessing, and tracking security and operational risks. Where appropriate, risks are mitigated through technical controls, process controls, and vendor management." 
Notes: Avoid naming a specific framework unless requested; if asked, cite SOC 2 control themes and internal risk program.

1.5 ✅ Independent assurance (SOC 2)
"Redwood undergoes independent SOC 2 assessment. SOC 2 reports can be made available to customers and prospects under NDA via our evidence request process."

1.6 ⛔ ISO / 27001 claims (do-not-overstate)
Do NOT say: “Redwood is ISO 27001 certified” unless explicitly confirmed by GRC for the current period.
Use instead:
"Redwood aligns many elements of its security program to common industry standards. If your RFP references ISO/IEC 27001, we can provide an alignment summary describing how key Annex A themes map to Redwood controls."

==============================
2) DATA PROTECTION / PRIVACY / DATA HANDLING
==============================

2.1 ✅ Customer data use & model training
"Redwood does not use customer prompts, inputs, or outputs submitted to the Redwood Inference service to train Redwood-owned or third-party foundation models. Customer data is processed solely to provide and maintain the service, including for security, reliability, and debugging consistent with customer configuration and contractual terms." 
Notes: If customer asks about ‘human review’ or ‘labeling’, route to retention/logging section; do not create new claims.

2.2 ✅ Data classification (general)
"Redwood treats customer-submitted content (e.g., prompts and outputs) as confidential customer data. Access is restricted to authorized personnel and systems necessary to operate the service, and access is logged and monitored."

2.3 ✅ Data minimization
"Redwood is designed to process only the data necessary to fulfill inference requests and operate the service. Customers control what they send to the service and should avoid submitting unnecessary sensitive data when possible."

2.4 ✅ Data residency (deployment-mode aware)
HOSTED / DEDICATED:
"Redwood offers regional deployment options for processing and service operation. Data residency commitments depend on the selected region(s) and configuration. We will describe the regions used for processing and storage for your account during solution design."
PRIVATE (VPC / on-prem):
"In Private deployments, customers control the environment where data is processed (e.g., customer VPC or on-prem). Data residency is determined primarily by the customer-controlled infrastructure location and configuration."
Notes: Do not promise ‘EU-only’ unless explicitly configured and confirmed for the requested scope; include caveats for support access and telemetry depending on config.

2.5 ✅ Data retention & deletion (high-level)
"Retention and deletion behavior varies by deployment mode and customer configuration. Redwood supports customer requests and configuration options to manage retention of prompts/outputs and operational logs consistent with our documentation and contractual terms."
Add if asked for detail:
"For details, refer to our customer-facing data retention and deletion overview; Redwood can also provide account-specific configuration guidance during implementation."

2.6 ⚠️ Personal data / GDPR
"Redwood supports customers in meeting applicable privacy obligations through contractual terms (e.g., DPA where applicable) and technical/organizational measures (encryption, access controls, logging). Customers determine the content submitted to the service and remain responsible for ensuring they have a lawful basis for processing personal data."
Notes: Avoid stating we are a ‘processor’ or ‘controller’ in generic text unless Legal has approved for the specific deal; refer to DPA.

2.7 ✅ Data separation / tenant isolation
HOSTED:
"Redwood logically isolates customer workloads using service-level access controls and tenant scoping."
DEDICATED:
"Dedicated deployments provide isolated capacity for a single customer. The isolation model and boundaries are documented as part of the dedicated deployment design."
PRIVATE:
"Private deployments run within customer-controlled infrastructure, and isolation is managed by the customer environment and configuration in combination with Redwood software controls."

==============================
3) ENCRYPTION / KEY MANAGEMENT
==============================

3.1 ✅ Encryption in transit
"Redwood uses industry-standard encryption for data in transit (e.g., TLS) between clients and Redwood endpoints and between service components as applicable."

3.2 ✅ Encryption at rest
"Redwood encrypts data at rest for systems and storage that persist customer data and service logs, consistent with the deployment mode and configuration."

3.3 ⚠️ KMS / HSM and key ownership boundaries
HOSTED / DEDICATED:
"Redwood uses managed key management services to protect encryption keys. Key management details (including any customer-managed key options) depend on deployment mode and contractual scope."
PRIVATE:
"In Private deployments, customers typically control the underlying cloud account / on-prem key management and may integrate Redwood with customer key management systems depending on the environment."
Notes: Do not state ‘customer-managed keys are available’ unless confirmed for the deal and mode; if asked, escalate to Security + Solutions Engineering.

==============================
4) ACCESS CONTROLS (SSO / RBAC / SCIM / ADMIN)
==============================

4.1 ✅ Authentication (console + APIs)
"Redwood supports secure authentication for access to the Redwood Console and APIs. For enterprise environments, Redwood supports SSO via SAML 2.0 and enforces role-based access controls (RBAC) for administrative functions."

4.2 ✅ SSO (SAML)
"Redwood supports SAML 2.0 single sign-on for the Redwood Console with common identity providers (IdPs). SSO configuration is available for enterprise plans and may be required for Dedicated/Private deployments depending on the contract."

4.3 ✅ SCIM (user lifecycle)
"Redwood supports SCIM provisioning for automated user lifecycle management where enabled for the customer account."
Notes: If the RFP asks for specific IdP support, include [IDP] and confirm via the internal SSO/RBAC reference.

4.4 ✅ RBAC model (generic)
"Redwood implements RBAC to restrict administrative actions based on job role. Roles control access to organization settings, API keys, usage visibility, deployment configuration, and audit log access, depending on deployment mode and enabled features."

4.5 ⚠️ Least privilege and privileged access
"Administrative access is restricted to authorized personnel and granted based on least privilege. Privileged access pathways are monitored and logged." 
Notes: Do not commit to specific tooling (e.g., exact PAM vendor) in customer-facing RFP text unless approved by Security.

4.6 ✅ MFA
"Multi-factor authentication is supported for user access and may be enforced via SSO based on customer IdP policy."

==============================
5) AUDIT LOGGING / MONITORING
==============================

5.1 ✅ Audit logs availability
"Redwood provides audit logging for administrative and security-relevant events within the Redwood Console and platform. Audit logs help customers review configuration changes and access patterns."

5.2 ✅ Audit log contents (safe, non-exhaustive)
"Audit logs typically include event time, actor identity, action/event type, target resource, and outcome (success/failure), with additional contextual metadata depending on the event type."
Notes: Keep non-exhaustive; do not enumerate a field list unless pulled from the canonical audit logging overview.

5.3 ✅ Export / SIEM integration (high level)
"Redwood supports mechanisms to export or integrate audit logs with customer monitoring and SIEM workflows, depending on deployment mode and contract."
Notes: If the RFP requires a specific destination (e.g., Splunk, S3, Sentinel), use: "We can review your target destination ([SIEM DESTINATION]) and confirm the supported export path during implementation." Avoid hard promises.

5.4 ⚠️ Retention of logs
"Audit log retention is configurable depending on plan and deployment mode. Redwood can support extended retention options as part of enterprise/compliance packaging." 
Notes: Do not quote exact default retention numbers in this master draft; instead reference the retention overview and align with pricing/packaging guidance.

5.5 ✅ Monitoring (Redwood side)
"Redwood monitors the service for availability, performance, and security signals. Monitoring supports incident detection and operational response."

==============================
6) SECURE SDLC / VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT
==============================

6.1 ✅ Secure development practices
"Redwood incorporates security into the software development lifecycle, including code review practices and security-focused testing activities appropriate to the system and risk."

6.2 ⚠️ Vulnerability scanning
"Redwood performs vulnerability management activities including scanning and remediation processes."
Notes: Do not state frequencies (e.g., ‘weekly’) or SLAs unless confirmed. If asked for patch timelines, use the remediation block below.

6.3 ⚠️ Remediation timelines (generic)
"Redwood prioritizes and remediates vulnerabilities based on severity, exploitability, and operational risk. Customers may report security issues via Redwood support channels or a designated security contact."
Notes: If the customer requires contractual SLAs for critical vulnerabilities, escalate to Security + Legal.

6.4 ⚠️ Penetration testing
"Redwood conducts periodic third-party security testing of relevant systems. A summary letter or attestation may be available under NDA through the evidence request process."
Notes: Do not specify frequency or scope unless provided by GRC for the relevant period.

6.5 ✅ Vulnerability disclosure / reporting
"Redwood accepts vulnerability reports and coordinates triage and remediation. If you have a security concern, contact Redwood through our established security reporting channel or via your account team who will route to Security."

==============================
7) INCIDENT RESPONSE / BREACH NOTIFICATION / BCP
==============================

7.1 ✅ Incident response program
"Redwood maintains an incident response process to triage, investigate, contain, eradicate, and recover from security incidents. The process includes internal escalation procedures and post-incident review."

7.2 ⚠️ Customer notification
"Redwood will notify customers of a confirmed security incident affecting customer data in accordance with contractual terms and applicable law." 
Notes: Do not quote notification timeframes (e.g., 72 hours) unless the contract specifies and Legal approves.

7.3 ✅ Business continuity / availability
"Redwood designs the platform for reliability and operational resilience, with monitoring and operational runbooks supporting service continuity."
Notes: If an RFP asks for specific RTO/RPO, escalate; do not invent numbers.

==============================
8) SUBPROCESSORS / VENDOR MANAGEMENT
==============================

8.1 ✅ Subprocessor transparency
"Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors that may process customer data to deliver the service (e.g., infrastructure providers). The current list can be provided through the appropriate customer-facing channel and/or under NDA where required."
Notes: Do not paste an outdated list into an RFP; link to canonical subprocessor list process.

8.2 ✅ Vendor risk management (general)
"Redwood evaluates vendors and subprocessors based on security and privacy risk, and applies contractual and technical measures appropriate to the service they provide."

==============================
9) DEPLOYMENT MODES / SHARED RESPONSIBILITY (HELPER BLOCKS)
==============================

9.1 ✅ Hosted API (Redwood-managed) shared responsibility snippet
"In Hosted API deployments, Redwood manages the underlying infrastructure and core service operations. Customers are responsible for secure usage of the service, including access to their Redwood account, appropriate handling of API keys, and decisions about what data to submit for processing."

9.2 ✅ Dedicated shared responsibility snippet
"In Dedicated deployments, Redwood provides isolated capacity for the customer and manages the service runtime consistent with the agreed architecture. Customers remain responsible for application-layer security, user access governance within their organization, and secure handling of credentials."

9.3 ✅ Private (VPC / on-prem) shared responsibility snippet
"In Private deployments, Redwood software is deployed into customer-controlled infrastructure (VPC or on-prem). Customers control network policies, perimeter security, and many operational controls in the hosting environment. Redwood provides guidance on secure configuration and supports the software per the contract."

==============================
10) COMMON QUESTIONNAIRE Q&A (SHORT PASTE BLOCKS)
==============================

10.1 ✅ "Do you store customer prompts/outputs?"
"Retention depends on deployment mode and customer configuration. Redwood can support configurations that minimize or restrict retention of prompts/outputs, and we document retention/deletion behavior and controls. We can confirm the applicable behavior for your deployment design and contract."

10.2 ✅ "Do you sell customer data?"
"No. Redwood does not sell customer data."

10.3 ✅ "Do you use customer data to train models?"
"No. Redwood does not use customer prompts/inputs/outputs to train models."

10.4 ✅ "Do you support SSO?"
"Yes. Redwood supports SSO via SAML 2.0 for the Redwood Console for enterprise deployments."

10.5 ✅ "Do you support RBAC?"
"Yes. Redwood supports role-based access controls (RBAC) for administrative functions."

10.6 ✅ "Do you provide audit logs?"
"Yes. Redwood provides audit logs for administrative and security-relevant events, and supports exporting logs depending on deployment mode and contract."

==============================
11) EXCEPTIONS / ALTERNATIVES (WHEN WE DO NOT MEET A CONTROL)
==============================

11.1 ✅ Standard exception language (use when needed + escalate)
"If a specific control is not available in the current Redwood offering for your selected deployment mode, Redwood can propose an alternative approach (e.g., compensating controls, customer-implemented controls in Private deployments, or contractual commitments where appropriate). Please share the exact requirement text and intended deployment mode so we can respond accurately."

11.2 ✅ Escalation note (internal)
- If you use exception language, open an internal review with Security/GRC and attach the customer requirement.
- Do not negotiate security addendum language without Legal.

==============================
12) INTERNAL NOTES / TODO (WORKING)
==============================
- TODO: Add a “Private deployment security appendix” block set (networking, logging boundaries, customer-managed KMS specifics) once SE + Security sign off. (Ref: Slack thread requesting appendix; Linear PM-4829)
- TODO: Confirm what we can safely say about audit log export destinations and what is GA vs ‘available with support engagement’. Align with docs PR-2849.
- TODO: Replace any remaining ambiguous retention phrasing with the canonical language from the retention overview and docs PR-2860.
- TODO: Add a short block about “data masking / redaction” — only if it is an actual product feature; otherwise keep as customer responsibility.

CHANGE NOTES (DRAFT HISTORY)
- 2026-02-24: Updated ‘data residency’ and ‘retention/deletion’ sections to avoid absolute commitments; added ‘do not quote default retention numbers’ guidance.
- 2026-02-10: Added shared responsibility snippets by deployment mode; tightened ISO wording to “alignment summary” only.
- 2026-01-23: Initial compilation from field intake + prior FAQ snippets; marked items requiring Security/GRC confirmation.
